name: twisted-planter
why: The part ParCAD web opens first, so it has to build, and read right, on a stranger's first visit. Two bodies. The planter: a ruled star loft twisted 60° through nine sections, cut hollow by the same star inset 3 mm at the same section heights, with six drains set between the saucer's first ring of bumps. The saucer: a revolved dish with 37 smooth bumps in rings of 1, 6, 12 and 18 (six more per ring keeps neighbours equally spaced), each a revolved smootherstep profile 2.4 mm tall that leaves the floor level. between_bodies reads the planter touching the bumps and nowhere else; 245 faces is the planter's plus the dish's 7 and one per bump, so no bump was lost (see GOTCHAS.md, a union that drops solids). measure_wall_thickness reads the planter's wall at 2.0 mm with its rim edge rounded; on the sharp rim it reports hundredths of a millimetre at the edge itself, where the flared facet meets the flat top at an acute angle.
